en: Mount Mayon is a stratovolcano, not a shield volcano, which is why it has a steep, perfect cone instead of broad, gentle slopes.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines at 505 kilometers, not the Pasig River.
Lake Mainit in Mindanao is the deepest lake in the Philippines, reaching a depth of 223 meters, not Laguna de Bay.
The Philippine tarsier is not exclusive to Bohol because it also naturally inhabits the islands of Samar, Leyte, and Mindanao.
Palawan is geologically part of the Asian continental shelf, meaning it is not a volcanic island like the rest of the Philippine archipelago.
Taal Volcano is actually an island located within Taal Lake, which fills the massive crater of a prehistoric volcanic eruption.
Mount Pulag, the second highest peak in the Philippines, is a non-volcanic mountain formed by tectonic uplift rather than volcanic eruptions.
The Philippine Sea is located on the eastern side of the country, bordering the Pacific Ocean, not the western side.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is located in the Sulu Sea, not the Philippine Sea or the Pacific Ocean.
Although it is the highest peak, Mount Apo is classified as an inactive volcano, meaning it has no historical record of eruption.
The Philippines has five distinct climate types, meaning places like Baguio experience a cool dry season unlike the typical wet and dry climate of Manila.
Luzon is the largest and most populous island in the Philippines, not Mindanao, covering an area of over 109,000 square kilometers.
